Why the endpoints matter

The proof that whiskering by an equivalence induces an equivalence uses unitors, associators, and identifications of functors. Consequently, some intermediate comparisons have different endpoints. The relevant elementary fact is that composition with a fixed identification gives an equivalence between identification animae.

We work with the absolute categories and the structures of Sections 1.1–1.3. Write \(\beta \cdot \alpha \) for vertical composition, with \(\alpha \) applied first. Whiskering is denoted by \(\star \). An expression such as \(\beta \cdot -\) is a functor: the fixed identification is used as a constant input to vertical composition.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For functors \(f,g,h\colon C\to D\) and an identification \(\beta \colon g=h\), the functor \[ L_\beta \colon (f=g)\longrightarrow (f=h),\qquad L_\beta (\sigma )=\beta \cdot \sigma , \] is an equivalence, with inverse given by composition with \(\beta ^{-1}\). Likewise, for \(\alpha \colon f=g\), the functor \[ R_\alpha \colon (g=h)\longrightarrow (f=h),\qquad R_\alpha (\tau )=\tau \cdot \alpha , \] is an equivalence, with inverse given by composition with \(\alpha ^{-1}\).

Proof idea

For the first assertion, the two inverse calculations are \[ \beta ^{-1}\cdot (\beta \cdot \sigma )=\sigma , \qquad \beta \cdot (\beta ^{-1}\cdot \tau )=\tau . \] Reassociate, apply the corresponding inverse comparison, and remove the identity identification by a unit comparison. These calculations hold as identifications of functors on the relevant identification animae: apply the vertical laws to the universal input, keeping the fixed identification as a constant family. The right-composition assertion uses the right unit and the same inverse laws. Evaluating the composite functors also uses the substitution comparisons from Specializing coherence laws. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Let \(f,g,f',g'\colon C\to D\), with identifications \(\alpha \colon f=f'\) and \(\beta \colon g=g'\). Suppose that functors \[ u\colon X\to (f=g),\qquad v\colon X\to (f'=g') \] are equipped with an identification of functors on \(X\) \[ \overline \beta \cdot u=v\cdot \overline \alpha , \] where the bars denote constant families. Then \(u\) is an equivalence if and only if \(v\) is an equivalence.

Proof idea

After the substitution comparisons, the given identification reads \(L_\beta \circ u=R_\alpha \circ v\), with common target \((f=g')\). Both \(L_\beta \) and \(R_\alpha \) are equivalences by Supplementary Lemma 1. Apply the two-out-of-three property and invariance of equivalence under identification of functors, in either direction. □

Whiskering by an equivalence

Supplementary Corollary 3. If \(F\colon C\to D\) is an equivalence, then both functors \[ F\star -\colon (f=g)\longrightarrow (F\circ f=F\circ g) \] for \(f,g\colon B\to C\), and \[ -\star F\colon (h=k)\longrightarrow (h\circ F=k\circ F) \] for \(h,k\colon D\to E\), are equivalences.

Proof idea

Choose an inverse \(G\) of \(F\). For postwhiskering, consider three successive functors on identification animae: postwhiskering by \(F\), then by \(G\), then by \(F\) again. The first two compose to an equivalence: the associator comparison relates their composite to postwhiskering by \(GF\), the supplied identification \(GF=\mathrm {id}_C\) relates that to postwhiskering by the identity, and the unitor comparison relates the latter to the identity functor on \((f=g)\). At each step, Supplementary Lemma 2 handles the changing endpoints. The second and third functors also compose to an equivalence, using \(FG=\mathrm {id}_D\). Two-out-of-six now implies that the first functor is an equivalence. The prewhiskering proof uses the corresponding comparisons on the other side.

The comparisons for composite and identity whiskering are displayed in Whiskering and horizontal composition. Replacing \(GF\) by the identity uses fixed-outer interchange; the analogous change for prewhiskering uses fixed-inner interchange. □

Lifting a specified identification

Supplementary Lemma 4. Let \(F\colon C\to D\) be an equivalence and \(f,g\colon B\to C\). Every specified identification \(\delta \colon F\circ f=F\circ g\) admits an identification \(\widetilde \delta \colon f=g\) together with an identification \[ F\star \widetilde \delta =\delta . \] Moreover, for \(\sigma ,\tau \colon f=g\) and a specified identification \(p\colon F\star \sigma =F\star \tau \), there is an identification \(\widetilde p\colon \sigma =\tau \) equipped with a comparison between its image under postwhiskering by \(F\star -\) and \(p\). The corresponding assertions hold for prewhiskering by \(F\).

Proof idea

Apply a chosen inverse of the equivalence \(F\star -\) to the absolute object \(\delta \). Its inverse comparison, together with the associator and unitor, gives the specified image comparison. For the higher assertion, apply Supplementary Corollary 3 to the equivalence \(F\star -\) itself, and repeat the same lifting construction on the resulting identification animae. □

The image comparison is part of the conclusion. It is needed, for example, when a lifted identification must fill a prescribed square. Keeping it avoids replacing that square by an unspecified comparison with the same endpoints.
